articles.title: Amazing Results of CWG 2026 lead India now to the Asian Games 2026
articles.description: FRAGRANCE OF IDEAS The Commonwealth Games (CWG) 2026 which began on 23 July, 2026 came to a glittering close on 2-3 August 2026 at Glasgow, the capital city of Scotland (UK). The Indian contingent did its best under the circumstances and brought home 39 medals including 13 gold, 17 silver and 9 bronze. The flag and baton of the CWG were handed over to the Indian officials at the end of the closing ceremony in recognition of the fact that the next CWG in 2030 would be held in India at Ahmedabad. The Indian Olympic Association President, P.T. Usha, Javelin Throw Champion, Neeraj Chopra and the Dy. Chief Minister of Gujarat, Harsh Sanghavi received the flag and the baton with the deserved honour and protocol of the Games. This handover officially marked India taking charge to host the 2030 historic Centenary Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad. The first such games were held in Hamilton-Canada in 1930. Hosting the 2030 Games is expected to boost India's global sporting profile, accelerate world-class sports infrastructure development, and showcase the country's organisational capabilities on the international stage. It should also be seen particularly in context of the preparations for the Asian Games to be held in September this year in Japan followed by the Olympics to be held in the US in 2028. India had sent a contingent of 191 members headed by Chief de Mission Rohit Rajpal and Deputy Chief de Mission Ravi Bengani. The contingent included 126 athletes (77 men and 49 women) and 51 team officials to participate in the games. Those who participated included 32 competitors (22 men and 10 women) in Athletics, 15 representatives each in Boxing & Judo and 12 competitors in weightlifting. There were only 10 sports disciplines plus the para sports this time which surely impacted the results as well for India. Shooting, wrestling, archery, hockey, badminton and table tennis -the mainstay sports of India- which bring a lot of fortunes for it traditionally were not included in the games this time. Ever since the inception of CWG in 1930, India continued to participate in the games barring only three times including the first one. It got the best results in the CWG 2010 when the games were organised in Delhi. It stood second in the medal tally with 101 total medals including 38 gold, 27 silver and 36 bronze. The second best performance by India was in CWG 2002 at Manchester when it won 30 gold, 22 silver, 17 bronze with a total of 69 medals. The performance this time at Glasgow with a tally of 39 medals was also satisfactory and encouraging. It secured 5th place on the overall medal table of the games and the first place among the Asian countries in the CWG 2026. This time the boxers from India exhibited a great class and character; and made history by entering into the 10 final events of the discipline. It won seven finals and also got 7 gold medals and 3 silver medals. This is India's best ever boxing performance. The gold finishers for India included Jasmine Lamboria, Preeti Pawar, Sakshi Chaudhary, Priya Ghanghas, Arundhati Chaudhary, Sachin Siwach and Ankush Panghal. The champion weightlifter Mirabai Chanu secured gold in the 48kg women’s category. In this way, she was able to successfully achieve a historic third consecutive CWG title. Sharmila Dhankar won gold in the women’s shot-put F57, leading the record-making campaign for Indian para-athletes. Dilip Gavit won a historic gold in the men’s 100m T47 event with a game record time of 10.71 seconds. This is the men’s first-ever para-athletic gold at the CWG. Mohammed Basil got silver in the same category thus giving India a 1-2 finish in the finals. While Soman Rana won gold in the men’s shot-put F57 para-athlete event, Shubham Juyal got a silver medal in the same event. Shilpa Shyla secured a bronze medal in the women’s shot-put F57 para-athlete event following a successful appeal. Gulveer Singh created a new history and became the first Indian track and field athlete to win two individual medals at a single CWG (silver in 10,000m and bronze in 5,000m). The ace champion Neeraj Chopra alongside debutant Yash Vir Singh won silver and bronze respectively in the Javelin throw. Asmita Dey and Harsh Singh clinched first-ever gold in the Judo competition marking India’s strong entry into the elite club of the sports men and women of the discipline. These remarkable achievements of India at an international platform is the reflection of the sports policy of India coupled with the infrastructure development at a grass-root level. Training methodology, investment in the sports sector and the grooming of sports men and women at a tender age are basics to the development of sports in the modern context. Then there are centres of sports men and women in a number of states in India where special arrangements have been made to groom the budding talent under national and international experts of various games and sports. A number of the athletes revealed that they were fully supported by their state governments and also the big institutions in the country. Great international players like Virat Kohli have also sponsored some key athletes who have shown exemplary results. The scenario in India has drastically changed and improved in context of the athletes taking part in international competitions like CWG, Asian Games, Olympics and the other important competitions held intermittently. Big companies and other organisations have been coming forward to help and support the deserving talent in the country. The CWG overall medal table highlights the most successful nations in the history of the competition. Australia continues to lead the all-time standings with an incredible 2,773 medals, followed by England and Canada, while India proudly holds fourth place with 602 medals. The rankings reflect decades of excellence across multiple sports and generations of world-class athletes. Keeping in view the next CWG 2030, the government of India immediately after the announcement of the Centenary CWG 2030, being held in India, took a number of major initiatives to take India to developing modern infrastructure in this regard. The Gujarat government has allocated ₹1,331 crore to transform Ahmedabad into an Olympic-ready city. The investment is intended to strengthen India’s bid to host the 2036 Olympic Games as well. The project focuses on developing world-class sports infrastructure in India in the coming four years. The Asian Games are also about to start in Aichi Prefecture and Nagoya, Japan from 19 September to October 4 this year. In the previous edition of the games in 2022 at Hangzhou-China, India for the first time crossed the 100-medal mark. The performance marked India's highest-ever medal haul in the history of Asian Games with 28 gold, 38 silver and 41 bronze totalling 107 medals. India finished fourth on the overall medal table after China, Japan and Korea. With the kind of encouraging results from Glasgow, the Indian Olympic Association, Ministry of Sports, Sports Authority of India and the respective sports institutions in various states should be surely thinking big in regard to the Asian Games 2026. There will be 43 sports spanning 469 medal events in the 2026 Asian Games in Japan, therefore the preparations are also supposed to be of the same nature and the required standard. The Olympics 2028 at Los Angeles is a little far away issue but thinking and planning has begun in this regard at various levels. India’s records at the Olympics excepting in Hockey aren’t so great but over the last two decades, some important strides have been taken and those have given good results as well. There are some big names who have brought laurels for the country and themselves in the Olympics. Some of them are as follows. Major Dhyan Chand and Balbir Singh Sr. of Hockey are among the extra-ordinary Indian Olympic champions recognized globally. Besides them, who made a mark in their respective sports with Olympic medals for the last three decades include Lendre Peas, Karnam Malleswari, Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore, Abhinav Bindra, Vijendra Singh, Sushil Kumar, MC Mary Kom, Vijay Kumar, Saina Nehwal, Gagan Narang, Yogeshwar Dutt, Neeraj Chopra, PV Sindhu, Sakshi Malik, Mirabai Chanu, Shreejesh, Harmanpreet Singh, Ravi Kumar Dahiya, Lovlina Borgohain, Bajrang Punia, Manu Bhaker, Sarabjot Singh, Swapnil Kusale and Aman Sahrawat. India has till date in its Olympics history won 41 medals comprising 10 gold, 10 silver and 21 bronze. The results of the recently held CWG, Asian Games and the different international sporting and athletic events in favour of India beckon Indian sports, sports men and women and the government to focus on Olympic Games and their standards. Much needs to be done in this context regardless of the previous results. The present generations need to take inspiration from our civilizational roots which had sports as an essential element of its greatness and grandeur all along. The modern sports and competitions demand great planning, high thinking, ultra-modern technical knowhow, high-value infrastructural facilities & logistics, consistent practice and competitions on different geographic pitches. This has been well acknowledged by the Union Sports Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya. He has further reinforced these preparations on the ground, noting that multi-sport continental events serve as prime platforms for podium finishes rather than mere exposure tours. In this connection, Prime Minister Narendra Modi also expressed full confidence that Indian athletes will significantly surpass their previous records at the upcoming Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, emphasizing that the government will fully support the preparations on the ground. Hope to see bewildering results forthcoming in order to usher joy, pride, enthusiasm and happiness all around. (The author is a senior BJP & KP leader, Human Rights Defender and a columnist and can be reached at: ashwanikc2012@gmail.com )

articles.title: Government e-Marketplace rewrites rules of public procurement : Piyush Goyal
articles.description: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal on Monday said that from a gross merchandise value (GMV) of Rs 422 crore a decade ago to over Rs 1,55,000 crore today, the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) has rewritten the rules of public procurement. In a post on X, the minister informed that over 12.28 lakh Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs), including more than 2.25 lakh led by women, and over 42,000 startups are registered on the portal, proving that grassroots empowerment is not merely a slogan for the Government under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, but a genuine commitment. “Over the last 10 years, the platform has enhanced competition, improved price discovery, reduced procurement cycle times, generated significant savings for the Government, and strengthened accountability through end-to-end digital procurement,” said Goyal. He further stated that this has made government markets more accessible to MSEs, startups, women entrepreneurs, Self-Help Groups, artisans, and weavers, while championing the vision of Vocal for Local and Make in India. “The GeM is emerging as a key driver of self-reliance that is also strengthening the foundation of a Viksit Bharat,” the minister mentioned. The GeM, into its 11th year, connects more than 1.37 lakh government buyer organisations with nearly 25 lakh sellers and service providers. The focus is shifting towards a smarter and more integrated public procurement ecosystem with GeM, which was launched on August 9, 2016. Artificial intelligence and wider participation will further strengthen transparency, efficiency and governance. By connecting government demand with local enterprises, GeM advances ‘Vocal for Local’, ‘Make in India’ and inclusive economic growth. GeM continues supporting India's journey towards a digitally empowered and self-reliant economy, according to an official factsheet. Beyond facilitating transactions, GeM has become an important pillar of India's Digital Procurement Ecosystem. It provides a comprehensive digital marketplace with over 10,660 product categories and 350 service categories, meeting diverse government procurement needs.

articles.title: Measles outbreak in Bangladesh claims six more lives, death toll crosses 870
articles.description: Dhaka, Aug 9 (IANS) As many as six children died with measles-like symptoms in Bangladesh in 24 hours until 8 a.m. (local time) on Sunday, raising the total number of confirmed and suspected measles-related fatalities in 2026 to 873, local media reported. All the latest deaths were suspected measles fatalities in Bangladesh, according to the statement released by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS). Following the latest update, the number of laboratory-confirmed measles fatalities remained unchanged at 98, while the number of suspected measles-related fatalities rose to 775, the United News of Bangladesh (UNB) reported. During the 24-hour period, 988 new suspected measles cases were reported in Bangladesh, raising the total number of suspected measles cases nationwide to 136,320. During the same period, 75 new confirmed measles cases were reported, raising the cumulative number of laboratory-confirmed infections to 17,115. As Bangladesh continues to witness a sharp increase in measles cases, a leading international advocacy group has described the 2026 outbreak as one of the country’s worst public health crises in recent history, highlighting the concern that the disease is preventable through vaccination. In its latest report titled ‘Preventable Tragedy: Bangladesh's 2026 Measles Outbreak’, Canada-based Global Centre for Democratic Governance (GCDG) said that although the measles outbreak appeared sudden to the public, it was not an unexpected event from an "epidemiological perspective". The report noted that the crisis resulted from a combination of disruptions to vaccine supply and health programs in 2024-2025 during the former interim government led by Muhammad Yunus, along with missed routine vaccinations, cancellations of scheduled supplementary immunisation programmes, administrative delays in vaccine procurement, and a failure to promptly identify at-risk populations. According to GCDG, Bangladesh had long procured WHO-approved vaccines through the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF)'s international supply chain; however, the interim government replaced this system with an open tender procurement process. Citing UNICEF, the report said the agency repeatedly warned the interim government of a potential vaccine shortage through five to six formal letters and around 10 meetings held between 2024 and 2026. Referring to Expanded Programme on Immunisation (EPI) data reported by Bangladeshi daily Samakal, the GCDG noted that measles vaccination coverage fell to 56.2 per cent in 2025, the lowest level recorded between 2017 and 2025. It added that WHO later identified the nationwide stock-out of the measles-rubella (MR) vaccine in Bangladesh during 2024-2025 and the lack of regular vaccination as the main contributors to the decline in immunity among children and the 2026 outbreak "Overall, the nationwide spread of measles resulted from a combination of administrative and health-system failures, including the programmatic vacuum created under the interim government; disruptions in vaccine procurement, transportation, and supply; vaccine stock-outs and canceled EPI sessions; declining MR1 and MR2 coverage; an increasing number of children missing scheduled vaccinations; the absence of supplementary immunization programs; and the current government’s inadequate and inefficient medical response," the GCDG said. The organisation further said that the current Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) government failed to respond swiftly to "known and measurable risks" after coming to power earlier this year. Criticising the lack of transparency, the GCDG described "information opacity" as a distinct and serious failure of the current government's medical response during the measles outbreak. --IANS akl/vd
